newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Showers expected in key Brazil soybean areas - coops.
newsitem.headline: Showers expected in key Brazil soybean areas - coops.

text.p: Conditions were favourable in Brazil's key soybean growing regions and the early harvest was progressing as expected, cooperatives said.
Scattered showers were forecast this weekend in Rio Grande do Sul and Parana while Mato Grosso should see clear skies, although with the possibility of showers, growers said.

"Conditions are very good, soil moisture is normal and temperatures are moderate," said Joao Henrich, agronomist at the Cotriba cooperative in Ibiruba, Rio Grande do Sul state. "We're expecting a normal harvest here."
Meanwhile in Mato Grosso, the harvest of the so-called precocious cycle crop was continuing apace as the weather stayed mostly clear following heavy rains in January.
"We now have 20 to 25 percent harvested," said Tony Fagundes at the Cooperlucas cooperative. "The harvest progressed normally this week and there is no longer this apprehension of a crop loss."
There was some loss of quality in the first of the early cycle crop to be harvested, he said. "But the product we are harvesting now is good," Fagundes added.
Harvesting had also begun at the Camp cooperative in Prudentopolis, Parana state, although it was only two or three percent of the total crop.
"Most of the crop is in the seed formation stage," said agronomist Aniceto Bobato.
Temperatures there were 28 to 29 degrees Celsius, he added.
